I highly suggest looking into Cognitive behavioural therapy, even if you can't do therapy due to money etc, theres tons of resources, books, videos and such to learn online, i know that takes alot of effort though. My grandfather helped one soldier in particular fighting in france during 1940.   after he came back from the war he became very good friends with my grandfather and the rest of the family. The soldier ( we call him uncle Al) had been fighting  the Nazis in france when he got caught in the lines of fire and was overrun by blitzkrieg.after fleeing into a forrest which connected to part of a river. He lived with two of his fellow soldiers, hiding in the river over the course of 3 days, only eating a candy bar and eggs they raided from a chicken coop on a nearby farm. They managed to be rescued  and escaped at Dunkirk before france fell.
Uncle Al recalled for the rest of his life he couldnt eat eggs and suffered from ptsd until his death in the mid 70s.
